explain.say: The Earth is built in layers, like a peach. On the outside is the crust, a thin rocky skin from about 5 kilometres thick under the oceans to about 70 under big mountains.

Below is the mantle, nearly 2,900 kilometres of hot rock. It is solid, but so hot it flows very slowly, and that flow helps move the plates above.

faq.a: The crust is about 5 to 10 kilometres thick under the oceans and about 30 to 70 kilometres under the continents, thickest under big mountain ranges. Compared to the whole Earth it is thinner than an apple's skin.
No, it is almost all solid rock. But it is so hot that over millions of years it can flow slowly, like very thick putty, carrying heat and moving the plates.
asks: What is the mantle made of?

faq.q: Why is the outer core liquid?
faq.a: It is hot enough to melt iron, and the pressure is not high enough to keep it solid. Deeper in, the inner core is even hotter, but the crushing pressure squeezes the iron solid.
asks: Why is the inner core solid?

faq.q: How do we know what is inside the Earth?
faq.a: No one has drilled through the crust. Scientists study how earthquake waves bend, speed up, slow down or vanish as they pass through, which reveals the layers, plus clues from meteorites and the Earth's weight.
asks: Has anyone dug to the centre of the Earth?

faq.q: How far is it to the centre of the Earth?
faq.a: About 6,370 kilometres. The deepest hole ever drilled, the Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia, reached only about 12 kilometres.

facts: The Earth's radius is about 6,370 kilometres.
The Kola Superdeep Borehole reached about 12.3 kilometres, the deepest hole ever drilled.
The inner core is mostly iron and is estimated to be about 5,200 degrees Celsius.

quiz.say: Which layer of the Earth is liquid?
quiz.why: The outer core is liquid iron and nickel; S waves from earthquakes cannot pass through it.

wrong.2: The inner core is solid because of enormous pressure.
